newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine to OK plan to privatise alumina plant - Fund.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine to OK plan to privatise alumina plant - Fund.

text.p: Ukraine's government plans to grant final approval next week for privatisation of its largest alumina factory in the southern city of Mykolayiv, a State Property Fund official said on Thursday.

"The project for plant privatisation recommends putting 26 percent of shares up for sale, with about 31 percent going to the workers' collective which has leased the plant," said the state privatisation agency's deputy director Bohdan Butsa.
He said the government was expected to approve the plan on February 18.

Russia's two biggest aluminium smelters, Krasnoyarsk and Bratsk, said on Thursday they had broken off talks with MHZ because its prices were too high, and would seek to buy alumina outside the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS).

MHZ, which accounts for virtually all of Ukraine's alumina production and which sells 90 percent of its output to the Russian smelters, is on a list of more than 200 firms which Ukraine wants to privatise through strategic foreign investment.

Butsa said the balance in AT Mykolayivsky Hlynozemny Zavod (MHZ) would also be sold to workers and managers, to the public in exchange for privatisation certificates, and on the Ukrainian Stock Exchange.
"I would not want to say how these shares will be divided, because the final figures may change," Butsa said, who added that sale of shares could begin this year.
MHZ has forecast production of 1.2 million tonnes of alumina this year. It produced 1.06 million tonnes during the first 11 months of 1996, and 996,000 tonnes in 1995.
Part of the plant's output also goes to Ukraine's AT Zaprizhsky Aluminyovy Zavod (ZAZ) smelter, and it also planned to sell to Tajikistan.
